ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, with O as the center and the length of OP as the radius, an arc is drawn intersecting the negative x-axis at point A. Thus, the coordinates of point A are ($- \sqrt{17}$, 0). Given that the y-coordinate of point P is $-1$, what are the coordinates of point P?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line $PB\perp OA$ at point B, \\
$\because$ the coordinates of point A are ($-\sqrt{17}$, 0), \\
$\therefore$ OP=OA=$\sqrt{17}$, \\
$\because$ the ordinate of point P is $-1$, \\
$\therefore$ PB=1, \\
$\therefore$ OB=$\sqrt{OP^{2}-PB^{2}}=4$, \\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point P are $\boxed{(-4, -1)}$.
